newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA'S BRM CALLS 25,000 TNS SCRAP TENDER.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA'S BRM CALLS 25,000 TNS SCRAP TENDER.

text.p: Romania's Bucharest-based commodities exchange will call a tender to sell 25,000 tonnes of scrap iron this month, the exchange said.
The scrap came from old rolling stock, Bursa Romana de Marfuri (BRM) said in a statement.
The minimum starting price for a tonne of iron scrap offered in the international tender scheduled for September 25 had been set at $95, BRM said.
Bidders have until September 23 to submit offers.

Till mid-1996, Romania applied a full ban on scrap iron exports. But in July, the Balkan country set an export quota for scrap iron of 100,000 tonnes this year with plans to fully liberalise export of the commodity by 1998.
Scrap iron from the shipping sector and rolling stock would make the bulk of those exports, the industry ministry said.
Liberalisation of scrap iron exports is part of Romania's strategy to adapt its legislation to that of the EU internal market, in view of its possible membership. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
